edges.limitations: Models haploinsufficiency, whereas human DD-II alleles produce a mutant protein proposed to act dominant-negatively; the phenotype appears only in older mice and conflicts with the statement that loss of one Dspp allele causes no dental phenotype in mice. The primary-versus-permanent dentition contrast cannot be modelled in mice, which have a single dentition.

nodes.description: Abnormal dentin is laid down into the pulp space. In primary teeth the pulp chambers are obliterated by abnormal dentin; in permanent teeth the coronal pulp chamber is enlarged with narrow canals (thistle-tube or flame shape) and contains numerous pulp stones, progressing to pulp obliteration. How a DSPP defect leads to excess intrapulpal mineral deposition, rather than only to hypomineralized dentin, is not established.

nodes.description: Retained mutant DSPP forms Ca2+-dependent complexes with co-expressed normal DSPP and reduces its exit from the rER in a dose-responsive manner, a dominant-negative effect that lowers the amount of DSPP secreted into the dentin matrix. N-terminal DPP frameshifts leave a shorter acidic Ca2+-binding segment before the frameshift and are thought to capture wild-type DSPP less efficiently, allowing more normal protein to be secreted and producing the milder DD-II phenotype rather than dentinogenesis imperfecta.

nodes.description: A single germline pathogenic DSPP allele initiates DD-II. Most DD-II alleles are -1 frameshifts in the N-terminal third of the exon 5 region encoding the Ser-Ser-Asx repeats of dentin phosphoprotein (DPP), which replace the acidic repeat with a hydrophobic downstream sequence; a signal-peptide missense change (p.Asp6Tyr) and an intron 2 splice-acceptor variant (IVS2-6T>G) are also reported. More C-terminal DPP frameshifts tend to cause the more severe dentinogenesis imperfecta type II, with exceptions.

nodes.description: In odontoblasts, mutant DSPP fails to traffic normally through the secretory pathway. Frameshift DPP mutants carry a long hydrophobic tail that anchors them to rough endoplasmic reticulum (rER) membranes, leader-region mutants are retained in the rER, and the signal-peptide p.Asp6Tyr mutant fails to translocate into the endoplasmic reticulum at all.
